gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/initial recommended=1

This PR makes the importer refuse an import record that has no id before writing it, and adds the import validation spec; you are its author. The spec keeps two behaviors in scope: refusing records without an id, which is covered by a test showing the record is refused and nothing is written, and putting the line number in the import error, which this PR does not deliver yet.

One problem blocks merging: the spec requires the import error to name the line of the bad record, but the importer returns only the message and never works out a line number (src/importer.mjs:12). An operator importing a large file therefore cannot tell which record failed, and no test checks for a line number (test/importer.test.mjs:8). After merge, the spec asks the person merging to tag the release. No documented command was found for that step, so it will be listed for you to do by hand. The spec's staging and production checks are confirmed after deploy and are not part of this review.

I recommend deliver because the missing line number is a code change inside this PR that the repair can make and test.

Pick one:
1. deliver - add the line number to the import error with a test, rebase on main, watch the checks, and repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. assess - post the problem to the PR as a review and make no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree and leave the PR as it is.

Functionality held in both: the rejection is covered, the line number is a gap and the single blocker, and the staging confirmation is explicitly not judged. Entries held in both, and After makes it firmer with the explicit "Spec Integration entries - no outcome" line. To keep these, retain the wording that matches a marked ticket row once without judging it and that drops anything under the body's Integration heading from the claim list. Keep the tag step's "open" status clearly a post-merge step status, so it is not read as a coverage outcome. Two things to watch: the prose sentence "The spec's staging and production checks are confirmed after deploy and are not part of this review" is fine as is, but it should not grow into per-entry statements that read as dispositions; and the After evidence repeats the "gauntlet: gate=" header before the re-rendered menu, which Before did not, though this affects no fact here.
